title: Great GASPI Data Schema
perspective: Local Kashmiri Advocates / J&K Coalition of Civil Society / High Court Bar Association

control_zones.governing_authority: Government of India / Indian Army / J&K Police
control_zones.access_restrictions: Heavy military presence; security checkpoints for local civilians; internet suspension orders issued under Temporary Suspension of Telecom Services Rules (2017)
Military cantonments and fencing established on lands; double-row concertina wire fence with sensors; local population restricted from entering designated security zones
Security convoys restrict civilian movement on National Highway NH-44; blockades during security operations

demographics.notes: Total population of Jammu and Kashmir as per Census 2011 is 1,25,41,302. Muslim population constitutes approximately 68.31%, Hindu population 28.44%. Demographic changes following the 2019 revocation of Article 370 and issuance of domicile certificates to non-locals have been a source of concern for local Kashmiri communities.

named_high_ground_features.name: Pir Panjal Range
named_high_ground_features.functional_strategic_description: Controls movement corridors between Jammu and Kashmir Valley; strategic observation points over highways and valleys; position relative to Jhelum and Chenab basins

named_high_ground_features.name: Zoji La Pass
named_high_ground_features.functional_strategic_description: Strategic high-altitude pass connecting Kashmir Valley to Ladakh; control of movement corridor; critical for military logistics and troop movements

physical_barriers.name: Anti-Infiltration Obstacle System (AIOS) / Smart Fence
physical_barriers.temporal_variations: Constructed 2003-2005; smart fence integration underway with sensors and cameras; hybrid model adoption
physical_barriers.stated_justification: Indian Government justifies as anti-infiltration measure
physical_barriers.opposing_characterization: Local Kashmiri advocates characterize the fence as a tool of partition, separation, and restriction on movement and livelihoods for the local population

agriculture.notes: Conversion of apple orchards and saffron cultivation land (Pampore) due to military occupation or highway projects

environmental_degradation_incidents.incident_type: Dal Lake and Wular Lake Degradation
environmental_degradation_incidents.stated_justification: Official justifications focus on conservation measures
environmental_degradation_incidents.opposing_characterization: Local farmers and institutions express concerns over the destruction of Dal Lake and Wular Lake due to encroachment, pollution, and lack of effective conservation
Local concerns regarding forest loss and its impact on the environment and traditional livelihoods

airspace_and_spectrum.cellular_tech_allowed: Transition from 2G caps to 4G/5G rollout post-2021
airspace_and_spectrum.opposing_characterization: Local advocates characterize the longest internet shutdown (552 days after 5 August 2019) and ongoing restrictions as violations of communication rights and digital control that isolate Kashmir from the rest of the world

controlled_item_categories: Dual-use items subject to security controls
trade_and_dual_use_controls.transit_permit_regimes: Permit regimes; identity verification at checkpoints

checkpoints_and_gates.name: Jammu-Srinagar National Highway (NH-44) Security Checkpoints
checkpoints_and_gates.stated_justification: Security checkpoints to prevent infiltration and ensure safety
checkpoints_and_gates.opposing_characterization: Restrictions on civilian movement during security convoys on National Highway NH-44; blockades and fencing; forced rerouting of local traffic

utilities_and_energy_grid.debt_or_fiscal_transfer_mechanisms: Transfer of electricity outside the Valley by NHPC and NEPRA; local electricity deficits

jurisprudence_and_statutory_friction.preferred_or_prior_system_name: Article 370, Article 35A, Constitution of Jammu & Kashmir (1956)
enforced_statutes_cited: Amendments to the Land Revenue Act (allowing non-residents to purchase land)

landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.holding_or_standard: Constitution Bench upheld the revocation of Article 370
landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.official_legal_rationale: The Court accepted the Union's argument that Article 370 was a temporary provision
landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.opposing_characterization: Local advocates and the High Court Bar Association challenged the 2019 Act as unconstitutional, arguing it undermined the historical autonomy of the region and the special rights of local residents

documented_statutory_conflicts.enforced_clause_reference: Amendments to the Land Revenue Act (2019 Reorganisation Act)
documented_statutory_conflicts.preferred_or_prior_clause_reference: Article 35A, J&K Alienation of Land Act (1938)
documented_statutory_conflicts.conflict_description: Clause-by-clause conflict between the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act 2019 and the traditional land rights of local Kashmiri residents under Article 35A. The 2019 Act and subsequent amendments allowed non-residents to purchase land, effectively overriding the 1938 J&K Alienation of Land Act which restricted land ownership to permanent residents.
Conflict between the historical constitutional framework that granted special status and autonomy to Jammu and Kashmir and the 2019 revocation which made all central laws applicable to the UT

official_threat_assessments_or_attack_st.numbers_or_incidents: 4,064 people arrested from March 2010 to January 2011 under the PSA and AFSPA; Amnesty International estimates between 8,000 and 20,000 people have been detained under the PSA or AFSPA over the past 20 years.
552 days of internet suspension after 5 August 2019, one of the longest internet shutdowns in history
official_threat_assessments_or_attack_st.source: Local advocates and civil society reports

stated_administrative_or_security_ration.official_rationale: Security measures to prevent terrorist coordination and maintain law and order
stated_administrative_or_security_ration.opposing_characterization: Local advocates characterize internet shutdowns as violations of communication rights and digital control that isolate Kashmir from the rest of the world

stated_administrative_or_security_ration.measure: Public Safety Act (PSA), AFSPA, and UAPA
stated_administrative_or_security_ration.official_rationale: Security legislation necessary to maintain public order and prevent terrorism
stated_administrative_or_security_ration.opposing_characterization: Local advocates characterize AFSPA as a 'lawless law' that enables security forces to act with impunity; under AFSPA, prosecution of security personnel requires central government sanction, which is practically impossible. 93% of complaints regarding settler violence against Palestinians are closed without charges filed - local advocacy groups draw parallels to the impunity of security forces and settlers under AFSPA and related laws.

stated_administrative_or_security_ration.measure: Land Law changes (Reorganisation Act and amendments)
stated_administrative_or_security_ration.opposing_characterization: Local advocates characterize these changes as a threat to the demographic composition and cultural identity of Kashmir, enabling land alienation from the local population
